0.7.8.title: Linux on every distribution, and terminal fixes at the edges
paragraphs: Rune stopped depending on one glibc baseline. A self-contained runtime loader lets the same build start on every major Linux distribution, and terminal and web-fetch behaviour was brought in line with what people actually run.
points: Self-contained runtime loader for every major Linux distribution.
tmux 256-colour palettes render correctly.
web_fetch handles session cookies automatically.

0.8.0.title: Twenty model presets and one dialect normalisation
paragraphs: The provider catalogue grew to twenty calibrated model profiles, with room for a local endpoint of your own. Behind them sits one normalisation layer, so an OpenAI, Anthropic or compatible gateway endpoint is described the same way.
points: Twenty calibrated model presets, plus custom local endpoints.
API dialect normalisation shared by OpenAI, Anthropic and compatible gateways.

0.8.1.title: The session picker points at the right row
paragraphs: Two navigation faults are gone: the caret in the session picker was off by one row, and keyboard navigation could stop short while browsing earlier prompts and sessions.
points: Session picker caret uses 1-based indexing; no off-by-one row highlight.
Keyboard navigation no longer short-circuits while browsing prompt and session archives.

0.8.9.title: Compaction keeps architecture, admission keeps its order
paragraphs: Older history is now cleared without losing the facts a session is built on, and the admission queue holds its chronological order even when several terminal windows act at once.
points: Context compaction preserves essential architecture facts while clearing expired history.
Session admission queue and its ordering hold up against concurrent terminal windows.

0.9.0.title: A submitted prompt is acknowledged at once
paragraphs: Admission no longer leaves a person waiting in silence. A prompt is acknowledged immediately, before the engine begins the heavy work of the turn, and a session survives a daemon or host restart through its immutable event journal.
points: Session admission acknowledges a submitted prompt before the engine turn starts.
Session resumption across daemon and host restarts, backed by immutable event records.

0.9.1.title: Launch intent from the task, and thinking you can set
paragraphs: Whether a command runs in the foreground or in the background is now a planning decision made from the task's own dependencies rather than from a tool name. The same release made a model's thinking settings reachable: off, or a low effort level, through the gateway.
points: Contextual execution planning derives tool launch intent from task dependencies.
Reasoning controls switch thinking off or select a low effort level via model gateways.

0.9.2.title: Mouse selection behaves like a terminal
paragraphs: Selecting text with the mouse and copying it now follows the terminal's own conventions, including clearing a selection, with the caret keeping stable coordinates and no stray chrome on screen.
points: Mouse selection, copy and clear follow standard terminal behaviour.
Caret coordinates and visual boundaries stay stable without terminal chrome artefacts.

0.9.3.title: A manual script, and references you can open
paragraphs: An explicit `!` runs a whole multiline script through the permission gate with full access for that call, and a link or file reference in a command's output can be inspected and opened in the browser only when you ask for it.
points: `!` runs entire multiline scripts through the permission gate with full access for that call.
Terminal links and file references can be inspected and opened on request.

0.9.4.title: The preview shows the whole script
paragraphs: Before a manual `!` script is confirmed you see all of its lines, not a shortened first line. The script also keeps the conversation context and working directory that preceded it.
points: Multiline shell script previews show the complete command before confirmation.
Manual `!` commands keep preceding context and the active working directory.

0.9.5.title: Background output has somewhere to go
paragraphs: A process that runs and waits now streams its standard output and error into its own log files, and the engine recognises an interactive prompt on Linux PTY sessions instead of letting it look like silence.
points: Running and waiting processes stream stdout and stderr to dedicated log files.
Input-wait detection recognises interactive prompts in Linux PTY sessions.

0.9.6.title: The composer previews while you type
paragraphs: The first line of a prompt is shown in the composer as you type it, and cursor placement and soft wrapping were corrected for both wide and narrow terminals.
points: Real-time prompt streaming shows the first preview line in the composer.
Cursor positioning and soft-wrap rendering corrected on wide and narrow viewports.

0.9.7.title: Newlines are drawn, not jumped over
paragraphs: A multiline composer now writes an explicit newline indicator instead of letting raw line breaks move the terminal, and pasting a multiline shell command into the editor stays responsive.
points: Multiline composer shows explicit newline indicators rather than raw line breaks.
Better editing responsiveness when pasting multiline shell commands.

0.9.8.title: Unknown stays unknown in the context count
paragraphs: A byte count nobody verified is now treated as unknown rather than converted into a guessed model capacity, and the engine's background guidance explains why a shell polling loop costs tokens and how to wait for a notification instead.
points: Strict context accounting treats unverified byte counts as unknown, never as a guess.
Background guidance explains why polling loops waste tokens and how to wait instead.

0.9.9.title: One owner per instruction, and a footer that keeps its promises
paragraphs: Each system instruction block now has a single owner, so two sources can no longer contradict each other. The terminal footer keeps an armed Esc cancellation, a retry countdown and a permission confirmation visible while they matter.
points: Single ownership per system instruction block, removing contradictory guidance.
Footer preserves armed Esc cancellation, retry countdowns and permission confirmations.

0.10.0.title: A live update notice stays where you can see it
paragraphs: When a new build is handed over while you work, the notice stays pinned in the active session view instead of disappearing with a redraw, and the whole test gate began running on real Linux, macOS and Windows machines.
points: Live update notices stay pinned and visible in the active session view.
Cross-platform gate validated on Linux, macOS (Apple silicon and Intel) and Windows.

0.10.1.title: Official help can never be shadowed
paragraphs: The official help skill now installs somewhere a person's own skills can neither shadow nor overwrite it. Old upgrade directories are trimmed automatically so they stop filling the disk.
points: Official help skill installation is isolated from user skills.
Automatic pruning of old upgrade directories preserves local disk space.

0.10.3.title: Terminal output says what the program said
paragraphs: Echoed shell input is separated from what the program actually printed, so a copied result holds only the program's output, and a tool's action sentence keeps its description while it streams so the call stays auditable.
points: Terminal output separates echoed shell input from the program's own stdout.
Tool action sentences keep explicit descriptions for auditing during streaming.

0.10.4.title: Errors keep their own words, and repeats are counted
paragraphs: `/logs` shows a provider's original error text beside the engine's turn status instead of paraphrasing it, and the same call made again and again is noticed before it burns the request budget.
points: `/logs` keeps the original provider error text alongside the turn status.
Identical consecutive tool calls are tracked and flagged before the budget runs out.

0.10.5.title: Waiting is not the same as looping
paragraphs: The loop guard now tells waiting for a process notification apart from repeating a command that keeps failing, and a tool failure arrives with the recovery step that fits its category.
points: Loop guard distinguishes waiting for a notification from repeated command failures.
Error diagnostics carry immediate recovery advice for each failure category.

0.10.6.title: Tool results are data, warnings are notices
paragraphs: A tool result now carries nothing but its own data; a repetition warning travels as a system notice instead, on a widening cadence, and it tells you what to do: stop polling a background task, or change the approach.
points: Tool results stay pure data; repetition notices arrive as system notices on Cadence B.
Loop warnings carry actionable guidance instead of only naming the repeat.

0.10.7.title: The output ceiling comes from the provider
paragraphs: A gateway's output ceiling is now read from the provider's own `max_tokens` rather than from a low thinking budget, which had been cutting long answers short. Completions of more than ten thousand tokens now finish normally.
points: Output ceiling aligned with provider `max_tokens`, not the thinking budget.
Streaming completions up to 10,712 tokens verified without premature cutoff.

0.10.9.title: Memory, aliases and cookies
paragraphs: The project memory prompt now says plainly what memory is for and that it is kept across sessions. Tool arguments accept the aliases people actually type, a wrong path gets the nearest candidate, and web fetch carries session cookies through redirects by itself.
points: Project memory prompt states long-term retention across sessions.
Tool arguments accept common aliases, clamp action text and suggest the nearest path.
web_fetch handles session cookies across redirects without manual headers.

0.10.10.title: Fewer pointless polls, clearer file errors
paragraphs: The system prompt now explains what a background task depends on, so the model stops polling work that already runs. File tools answer a bad path with the nearest candidate and refuse a stale patch with guidance instead of a bare failure.
points: System prompt clarifies background execution dependencies to avoid redundant polling.
File tool errors carry nearest-path suggestions and stale-patch guidance.

0.11.0.title: No empty header over a blank response
paragraphs: A streamed response that began with whitespace or blank lines used to draw an empty `Response` header. The header is now drawn only when there is text, and the bytes themselves still pass through untouched, with no regex and no lossy stripping.
points: Empty response headers are gone when a response begins with whitespace or blank lines.
Flow transparency and exact byte fidelity kept; no regex or lossy stripping.

0.11.1.title: A repeated answer is stopped while it streams
paragraphs: The engine now recognises a response that repeats one short unit over and over and stops it as it arrives, with no ceiling on token length. You are then asked, in the form you already know, whether to keep the text written before the repeat or discard the message.
points: Engine-level repetition guard halts a repeating loop at 4 KiB, or 16 KiB for whitespace.
The clarification form keeps preceding prose or discards the corrupted output.
Normal streaming speed preserved, with no arbitrary token limit and no false positives on minified data.

0.11.2.title: Gaps that no longer hang
paragraphs: An intermediate response left dangling empty lines behind it, which pushed the next tool call down the screen. The trailing blank lines are trimmed and the spine between tool calls is now one consistent distance.
points: Dangling empty lines removed from intermediate responses in the renderer.
Vertical spacing between consecutive tool calls made uniform.

0.11.3.title: One tool for background processes
paragraphs: Background work is managed by one `process_control` tool with a `type` and a `stop` action. Two legacy tools are gone, so there is one place to look and no ambiguous choice of parameters, and a format-28 upgrade carries older session records over.
points: `process_control` unifies background management with `type` and `stop` actions.
`terminal_input` and `kill_task` removed, ending parameter ambiguity.
Format 28 upgrade moves older session records to the unified tool smoothly.

0.11.4.title: A notification that carries its own output
paragraphs: A background task's end now arrives as one self-contained notification: how it ended, its process id, and the output you had not been given yet, defused and bounded. It replaces the extra wake-up roundtrip that used to fetch those details, and a stop now reaches the whole process tree.
points: Notifications deliver defused process output in the event payload itself.
Metadata, exit code and recent lines travel in one packet, removing an auxiliary wake call.
Cleanup routines terminate the whole process tree without orphans.

0.11.5.title: First start, and Windows path patterns
paragraphs: Two faults found on real machines are fixed: on a first start the official help skill checked itself while the session was being created, and on Windows a path pattern ending in a dot or a space was not handled. The smoke suite also checks a clean-environment start on each platform.
points: First-start race between help-skill verification and session creation resolved.
Windows path patterns ending in a trailing dot or whitespace handled.
Smoke suite verifies clean-environment startup on POSIX and Windows.

0.11.6.title: What a manual script may do, said plainly
paragraphs: The manual shell screen now explains the execution boundary of an `!` command in words: what access it has, and that the classifier and sanitizer are bypassed for that one call. The wording matches what happens on POSIX shells and on Windows ConPTY.
points: Manual shell screen explains elevation and privilege boundaries of `!` commands.
Sanitizer and classifier bypass semantics clarified for POSIX and Windows ConPTY.

0.11.7.title: A thought is not split by the text that follows
paragraphs: Reasoning could arrive interleaved with the answer, so a sentence of thinking was cut in half by the first words of the reply. Reasoning deltas are now evaluated before text deltas, and the fragments of one round are coalesced, keeping a clean boundary before the final text.
points: Reasoning deltas evaluated strictly before text deltas, ending split thoughts.
Intermediate thought fragments coalesced per turn round.
Multi-hop handover child sessions are acknowledged before the parent host releases.

0.11.8.title: Switching mode mid-stream no longer redraws the footer
paragraphs: Changing permission mode while a response streams used to recalculate priorities and reflow the footer for no reason. A status notice you are reading now survives the switch, and the promises the footer makes stay intact in every window.
points: Changing permission mode during streaming no longer triggers false priority recalculations or footer reflows.
Active status notices are preserved during mid-stream mode switching.
Esc cancellation, linear retries and confirmation dialogs keep their priority in every window.

0.11.9.title: Grouped path patterns, searched in one call
paragraphs: find_files and the include filter of search_text now expand brace alternatives in a path, including nested groups, alongside `|` alternatives. A pattern like `*.{ts,tsx}` is one call over one directory walk rather than several, and no provider declaration changed to make that possible.
points: Brace alternatives such as `*.{ts,tsx}`, nested groups and `|` alternatives expand natively.
find_files and search_text's include filter search a grouped pattern in one call.
Expansion happens in the engine: no tool declaration and no database format changed.
